text:
Ethan (Finance): Heads up 1: AWS Marketplace invoice GJ-2028-05-01 has several NEGATIVE charge lines from a partner promotion. We need to decide if these are customer credits or vendor refunds. See sample below.

Sofia (Billing): Paste sample lines? Negative amounts usually mean proration/credits.

Ethan (Finance): Sample: `Invoice: GJ-2028-05-01
LineItem: marketplace:us-east-1:partner-CloudSprint:promo-credit  Qty: 1  ChargeUSD: -4500.00  attrs: {promo_code: SPRING_TRIAL, metering_id: ms-987654}`

Manny (Partnerships): CloudSprint rolled a pricing experiment for trial customers in April. They reported issuing downstream credits to end-customers, not billing us negative. Something may have flipped on their marketplace configuration that reversed the flow. I'm pinging their partner rep now.

pricing-bot: Automated scan: Negative marketplace credits = $4,500.00 across 3 lines on GJ-2028-05-01. Suggested actions: validate partner intent, check refund vs credit accounting treatment. Link: https://billing.internal/recon/GJ-2028-05-01

Will (SRE): Quick check: our ingestion shows partner_type=marketplace and charge_type=credit. No invoice tags indicating "vendor_refund". Transform currently treats negative charges as customer credits by default. Might need manual override.

Sofia (Billing): Accounting impact: if these are vendor refunds (we owe them money), we need a payable; if they are credits applied to customers, then it's contra-revenue. We should withhold making GL changes until partner confirms. Can we isolate affected customers?

Ethan (Finance): Yes. I ran match query against metering_ids: impacted customer set = 3 accounts. If partner confirms they intended vendor refunds, we will need to post: DR Vendor Receivable / CR Marketplace Revenue reversal. Otherwise DR Sales Refunds / CR Accounts Receivable.

Manny (Partnerships): CloudSprint replied: "We mistakenly flipped settlement direction on promo SKUs for April 20-25. We want marketplace to issue customer-facing credits, not negative billing to Redwood. We'll submit an adjustment to correct the invoice and reissue positive charges. Partner will cover any reconciliation effort"

Sofia (Billing): Good. So action is to ask AWS to reissue corrected invoice OR we can apply internal offset journal for month-close. Which is preferred?

Ethan (Finance): Prefer corrected invoice if possible. Request AWS invoice adjustment referencing GJ-2028-05-01 and partner case CS-4921. If they can't deliver before close, approve internal temporary journal: DR Marketplace Revenue 4,500.00 / CR CloudSprint Payable 4,500.00 with note "temp offset pending AWS invoice correction".

pricing-bot: Partner case opened CS-4921. AWS case link: https://aws.console/cases/CS-4921 (internal). Estimated adj ETA 7 business days.

Manny (Partnerships): CloudSprint asked us to go ahead with internal journal so they can proceed with customer credits immediately. They also asked for contact for reimbursement if any differences arise.

Sofia (Billing): Maria (Finance lead) needs to approve the temporary payable. @Ethan can you escalate?

Ethan (Finance): I'm looping Maria. Maria, please approve temporary payable journal up to $5k for GJ-2028-05-01 pending AWS correction.

Maria (Finance) (joined): Approved. Post temporary journal and tag as "mp-temp-payable" with reference GJ-2028-05-01 and partner CloudSprint.

Sofia (Billing): Journal posted: JRN-2028-05-12-078 DR Marketplace Revenue 4,500.00 / CR CloudSprint Payable 4,500.00. Tagged for month-close.

Will (SRE): Noting for runbook: transform should flag negative marketplace lines and add a "requires_partner_verification" tag to speed review. I'll submit a small PR to include that flag and add to monitoring.

Manny (Partnerships): CloudSprint confirmed they'll send a confirmation email and cover reconciliation labor. I'll attach correspondence to the case.

Ethan (Finance): Closing loop: we'll reverse the temp journal if AWS issues corrected invoice. Nina (RevOps) will run reconciliation when AWS update arrives. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
